import asyncio

import httpx

from app import service


async def _get(path):
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(app=service.app, base_url="http://test") as client:
        resp = await client.get(path)
        return resp.status_code, resp.json()


def test_health():
    assert asyncio.run(_get("/health")) == (200, {"ok": True})


def test_price_lookup():
    assert asyncio.run(_get("/price/pear")) == (200, {"item": "pear", "cents": 95})
    assert asyncio.run(_get("/price/kiwi")) == (404, {"error": "unknown item"})


def test_price_list():
    status, body = asyncio.run(_get("/prices"))
    assert status == 200 and body["items"] == ["apple", "fig", "pear"]

SIGNING_KEY = b"demo-signing-key"


def signed_order(client, order):
    """Build the order request and sign its exact body, as the rates API's order endpoint requires."""
    import hashlib
    import hmac

    request = client.build_request("POST", "/orders", json=order)
    body = request.read()
    request.headers["X-Signature"] = hmac.new(SIGNING_KEY, body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return request

def test_signed_order_signature_matches_body():
    import hashlib
    import hmac

    with client() as c:
        req = rates.signed_order(c, {"sku": "A-1", "qty": 2})
    # A weak test, as real suites often are: it checks the signature against whatever body was sent.
    expected = hmac.new(rates.SIGNING_KEY, req.content, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    assert req.headers["X-Signature"] == expected

change.behaviour: signed_order(): client.build_request('POST', '/orders', json=order).read(). httpx 0.23.3 serialises json= with json.dumps defaults: b'{"sku": "A-1", "qty": 2}' (24 bytes); 0.28.1 uses compact separators and ensure_ascii=False: b'{"sku":"A-1","qty":2}' (21 bytes), so the HMAC signature (and Content-Length) differ. The test only checks the signature against whatever body was built.

notes: httpx 0.23.3 (Python 3.11) -> 0.28.1 (Python 3.12), the newest release. A public-API diff (every signature in httpx.*) finds only proxies=/app= removed from Client/AsyncClient, proxies=/cert= removed from the top-level helpers, and create_ssl_context(http2=) removed; everything else that changes is behaviour. Jumping 0.23 -> 0.28 skips the whole deprecation runway: 0.23.3 emits NO warning for proxies=, app= or verify=<str> (they were deprecated in 0.26, 0.27 and 0.28), so expected_warnings is empty and old-side warnings cannot help. The new-side verify=<str> DeprecationWarning is removed by manual_migration, so the post-migration capture does not see it. Offline: httpx.MockTransport for the remote rates API, AsyncClient over the in-process ASGI app for the service (the FastAPI test pattern). The mock answers with content=json.dumps(...) rather than httpx.Response(json=...): Response(json=) is compact in 0.28 too, so a json= mock would change the response bytes in the equiv scenario as well; the change scenario keeps that behaviour change to itself. Checked and deliberately NOT ground truth: charset fallback (0.23.3 already defaults to utf-8 when charset_normalizer is absent, which it is: httpx 0.23 does not depend on it), query-param encoding (None, bools, floats, lists, non-ASCII: identical), URL joining, Timeout repr, HTTPStatusError text (its help link moved from httpstatuses.com to developer.mozilla.org; the app reads status and body only). manual_migration edits 1-3 are one change (proxies -> mounts plus the ssl import used by edit 4); leaving out edit 4 alone passes with the verify DeprecationWarning, which is what DEPRECATED means here. raise_for_status() is listed as BEHAVIOR because its return value really changed (None -> the Response, from 0.25), but every call in the app discards it, so the equiv scenario still expects PASS: a verify FAIL on it is a false alarm for this app.
